title: Biliary Tract Cancers
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2026 clinical navigator for Biliary Tract Cancers (Gallbladder Cancer, Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma, Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma). Implements Workup First diagnostic checklists, resectability triage, BILCAP adjuvant capecitabine, TOPAZ-1 / KEYNOTE-966 frontline chemoimmunotherapy, and subsequent line NGS biomarker-directed therapies (FGFR2, IDH1, HER2, BRAF, MSI-H). References StewardMD ONCQIS Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Biliary Tract Cancers Version 1.2026 (March 10, 2026).

a.text: CA 19-9 is falsely elevated by biliary obstruction and cholangitis; draw baseline after biliary decompression. Approximately 5-10% of patients are Lewis-antigen negative (Le a-b-) and cannot synthesize CA 19-9, so a normal value never excludes malignancy.

b.text: Staging laparoscopy with laparoscopic ultrasound detects occult peritoneal or superficial liver metastases in 20-30% of gallbladder cancers and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinomas judged resectable on imaging, sparing nontherapeutic laparotomy (BIL-1, BIL-2).

c.text: BILCAP phase III: adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 twice daily days 1-14 every 21 days for 8 cycles after macroscopically complete resection improved median overall survival (51.1 vs 36.4 months per-protocol; ITT 49.6 vs 36.1 months). NCCN Category 1 preferred adjuvant therapy.

d.text: TOPAZ-1 (gemcitabine + cisplatin + durvalumab) and KEYNOTE-966 (gemcitabine + cisplatin + pembrolizumab) each improved overall survival versus gemcitabine + cisplatin alone in advanced biliary tract cancer. Both chemoimmunotherapy combinations are NCCN Category 1 preferred first-line options for eligible patients.

e.text: ABC-06 phase III: mFOLFOX6 plus active symptom control improved median overall survival versus symptom control alone (6.2 vs 5.3 months) after progression on gemcitabine + cisplatin, establishing mFOLFOX6 as the standard biomarker-negative second-line regimen.

f.text: FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements (pemigatinib, FIGHT-202; futibatinib, FOENIX-CCA2) and IDH1 R132 mutations (ivosidenib, ClarIDHy) occur predominantly in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. Test at diagnosis of unresectable or metastatic disease so targeted therapy is ready at progression; repeat biopsy or ctDNA at acquired resistance.

g.text: Future liver remnant (FLR) thresholds: portal vein embolization is indicated when anticipated FLR is below 30% in normal liver or below 30-40% in cholestatic, steatotic, or cirrhotic liver. Re-image in 3-4 weeks to confirm hypertrophy before extended hepatectomy.

nodes.name: Histology
nodes.title: Biliary Tract Cancer: Anatomic Site and Presentation
nodes.description: Step 1: Clinical Presentation. Select the confirmed primary site and presentation of biliary tract cancer.
bullets: Gallbladder Cancer (GBC): gallbladder mass or wall thickening on imaging, gallbladder polyp meeting resection criteria, or incidental carcinoma found on routine cholecystectomy pathology (BIL-1).
Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA): intrahepatic liver mass with peripheral rim enhancement, capsular retraction, and biliary dilation; second most common primary liver cancer (BIL-2).

Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma (eCCA): perihilar (Klatskin) stricture at or above the cystic duct insertion, or distal stricture below the insertion with painless obstructive jaundice (BIL-3, BIL-4).
Advanced disease: biopsy-proven unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic biliary tract adenocarcinoma of any primary site.

options.label: Gallbladder cancer (mass, polyp, or incidental cholecystectomy finding)
Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA, liver mass)
Extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (eCCA, perihilar or distal stricture)
Known unresectable, locally advanced, or metastatic BTC (any site)

nodes.name: GBC workup
nodes.title: Gallbladder Cancer: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Complete staging workup before any resectability decision. Confirm adenocarcinoma, exclude occult peritoneal seeding, and relieve obstruction.
bullets: Multiphase contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT or liver MRI with MRCP: defines depth of gallbladder wall invasion, liver infiltration (segments IVB/V), vascular involvement, and nodal disease.
Serum CA 19-9 and CEA at baseline; repeat CA 19-9 after biliary decompression because obstruction falsely elevates it.

EUS with FNA or ERCP with brush cytology, FISH polysomy testing, or forceps biopsy for tissue confirmation when imaging is equivocal; endoscopic or percutaneous biliary drainage for obstructive jaundice or cholangitis before any systemic therapy.
Staging laparoscopy with laparoscopic ultrasound for all potentially resectable gallbladder cancers to rule out occult peritoneal seeding and superficial liver metastases.
Chest CT to complete metastatic survey; medical operability assessment and multidisciplinary hepatobiliary tumor board review.

For unresectable or metastatic disease: mandatory comprehensive molecular testing (NGS panel with FISH/IHC) covering FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, IDH1 R132 mutations, HER2/ERBB2 amplification, BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, NTRK fusions, RET fusions, and TMB-H.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: iCCA workup
nodes.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Complete staging workup before any resectability decision. Distinguish iCCA from HCC, establish margin-negative resectability, and secure tissue for molecular testing.
bullets: Multiphase contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT or liver MRI with MRCP: characterizes mass-forming, periductal-infiltrating, or intraductal growth; maps multifocality, satellite nodules, and vascular invasion.
Serum CA 19-9 and CEA; add AFP when HCC is in the differential (cirrhotic liver, arterial hyperenhancement with washout favors HCC).

Core-needle liver biopsy with immunohistochemistry when imaging is atypical or systemic therapy is planned; EUS/ERCP with brush cytology, FISH polysomy, or biopsy for periductal components; biliary drainage for obstructive jaundice or cholangitis.
Staging laparoscopy with laparoscopic ultrasound for potentially resectable iCCA to rule out occult peritoneal seeding and surface metastases.
Chest CT, assessment of chronic liver disease and future liver remnant, and multidisciplinary hepatobiliary tumor board review.

For unresectable or metastatic disease: mandatory comprehensive molecular testing (NGS panel with FISH/IHC) covering FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, IDH1 R132 mutations, HER2/ERBB2 amplification, BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, NTRK fusions, RET fusions, and TMB-H.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: eCCA workup
nodes.title: Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Complete staging workup before any resectability decision. Classify the stricture level, secure a tissue diagnosis, and decompress the obstructed system.
bullets: Multiphase contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT or liver MRI with MRCP: defines stricture level (perihilar versus distal), longitudinal ductal extent, vascular encasement, lobar atrophy, and nodal disease.
Serum CA 19-9 and CEA; repeat CA 19-9 after biliary decompression because obstruction falsely elevates it.

EUS with FNA plus ERCP with brush cytology, FISH polysomy testing, or intraductal forceps biopsy; EUS is preferred for distal strictures and nodal sampling. Biliary drainage (endoscopic stent first line) for obstructive jaundice, cholangitis, or planned major hepatectomy.
Bismuth-Corlette mapping for perihilar tumors (types I-IV) with dedicated cholangiographic imaging; volumetric future liver remnant assessment when hepatectomy is contemplated.
Chest CT, IgG4 level when benign sclerosing disease is possible, and multidisciplinary hepatobiliary tumor board review.

For unresectable or metastatic disease: mandatory comprehensive molecular testing (NGS panel with FISH/IHC) covering FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, IDH1 R132 mutations, HER2/ERBB2 amplification, BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, NTRK fusions, RET fusions, and TMB-H.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: Advanced BTC workup
nodes.title: Unresectable or Metastatic BTC: Workup and Molecular Checklist
nodes.description: Confirm fitness for first-line chemoimmunotherapy and complete mandatory molecular profiling that drives subsequent-line targeted therapy.
bullets: Multiphase contrast-enhanced abdominal and pelvic CT or liver MRI with MRCP plus chest CT: documents measurable disease (RECIST 1.1 baselines) and rules out actionable obstruction.
Serum CA 19-9 and CEA; repeat CA 19-9 after biliary decompression because obstruction falsely elevates it.
EUS/ERCP with brush cytology, FISH polysomy, or biopsy when primary tissue is still needed; urgent biliary drainage for obstructive jaundice or cholangitis before systemic therapy starts.
Performance status, comorbidity review (autoimmune history, interstitial lung disease, organ function, hearing and renal baselines for platinum), and goals-of-care discussion.

Mandatory comprehensive molecular testing (NGS panel with FISH/IHC) before or concurrent with first-line therapy: FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements, IDH1 R132 mutations, HER2/ERBB2 amplification, BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, NTRK fusions, RET fusions, and TMB-H.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Resectability Staging

nodes.name: GBC staging
nodes.title: Gallbladder Cancer: Presentation and Resectability
nodes.description: Stratify by how the cancer presented and whether an R0 resection is technically feasible at a high-volume hepatobiliary center.
bullets: Incidental GBC: carcinoma discovered on routine cholecystectomy pathology; depth of invasion (pT1a versus pT1b or greater) decides between surveillance and radical re-resection.
Upfront resectable: gallbladder mass or polyp without distant metastases, without major vascular encasement, and with adequate future liver remnant for segments IVB/V resection.
Locally advanced unresectable: extensive liver infiltration, bilateral vascular involvement, bulky N2 nodes, or inadequate remnant that precludes R0 resection.
Metastatic: distant liver metastases beyond contiguous infiltration, peritoneal seeding, or extra-abdominal spread.

options.label: Incidental GBC on cholecystectomy pathology
Upfront resectable gallbladder mass or polyp
Locally advanced unresectable disease
Metastatic disease

nodes.name: Incidental GBC depth
nodes.title: Incidental GBC: Depth of Invasion on Pathology
nodes.description: Pathologic T stage of the cholecystectomy specimen determines whether simple cholecystectomy suffices or radical re-resection is required.
bullets: pT1a (invasion into lamina propria only): simple cholecystectomy with negative cystic duct margin is adequate definitive therapy.
pT1b or greater (invasion into or through muscularis propria): requires radical re-resection with liver wedge and portal lymphadenectomy once staging is complete.
Review cystic duct margin, perineural and lymphovascular invasion, grade, and nodal harvest from the index operation; re-image before re-resection to exclude interval dissemination.

options.label: pT1a (lamina propria only), cystic duct margin negative
pT1b or greater (muscularis propria invasion or deeper)

nodes.name: T1a GBC complete
nodes.title: Incidental pT1a GBC: Simple Cholecystectomy and Surveillance
nodes.description: Definitive local therapy is already complete; no further resection or adjuvant therapy is indicated.
bullets: No radical re-resection: simple cholecystectomy with a negative cystic duct margin is curative for pT1a disease with 5-year survival above 95%.
No adjuvant systemic therapy or radiation is indicated for completely resected pT1a N0 gallbladder cancer.
Surveillance: history, physical, liver function tests, and CA 19-9 every 6 months for 2 years then annually; contrast-enhanced imaging every 6-12 months for 2 years.

nodes.name: T1b+ radical re-resection
nodes.title: Incidental pT1b+ GBC: Radical Re-resection
nodes.description: En bloc liver wedge resection of segments IVB/V with portal lymphadenectomy, then margin-directed adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Radical re-resection at a high-volume center: en bloc wedge resection of gallbladder fossa (segments IVB/V with at least 2 cm margin) plus standard portal lymphadenectomy of the hepatoduodenal ligament (examine at least 6 nodes).
Resect residual port sites only if there was intraoperative bile spillage or documented port-site disease; routine port-site excision is not required.
Record margin status (R0 versus R1), nodal yield, and perineural invasion on synoptic pathology; proceed to margin-directed adjuvant therapy.

options.label: Re-resection completed - proceed to margin-directed adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: GBC radical resection
nodes.title: Resectable GBC: Radical Cholecystectomy
nodes.description: Upfront radical resection for gallbladder mass or polyp judged resectable on workup and staging laparoscopy.
bullets: Radical (extended) cholecystectomy: en bloc gallbladder removal with wedge resection of segments IVB/V (at least 2 cm liver margin; formal right hepatectomy only for extensive infiltration) plus portal lymphadenectomy with at least 6 nodes examined.
Intraoperative frozen section of the cystic duct stump; extend to bile duct resection with Roux-en-Y reconstruction when the stump is positive.
Avoid intraoperative bile spillage; convert promptly when anatomy is unfavorable. Record R0 versus R1 status for adjuvant planning.

options.label: Resection completed - proceed to margin-directed adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: iCCA staging
nodes.title: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: Resectability Assessment
nodes.description: Resectability requires a solitary tumor (or confined disease) amenable to margin-negative anatomic resection with adequate future liver remnant and no extrahepatic spread.
bullets: Resectable: solitary mass without major vascular invasion, no multifocal or bilobar satellites, no suspicious extrahepatic nodes or distant metastases, and adequate future liver remnant.
Unresectable: multifocal or bilobar disease, major vascular invasion not amenable to reconstruction, inadequate remnant despite PVE, cirrhosis with prohibitive operative risk, or distant metastases.
Staging laparoscopy findings of peritoneal seeding or surface metastases convert resectable imaging into unresectable disease.

options.label: Resectable: solitary tumor, R0 feasible, adequate remnant
Unresectable, multifocal, vascular invasion, or metastatic

nodes.name: iCCA resection
nodes.title: Resectable iCCA: Anatomic Liver Resection with Lymphadenectomy
nodes.description: Anatomic hepatectomy with negative margins and regional lymphadenectomy, then margin-directed adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Anatomic liver resection (segmentectomy, sectionectomy, or hemihepatectomy) with a goal of microscopically negative (R0) margins of at least 1 cm; non-anatomic wedge resection is discouraged for mass-forming iCCA.
Regional portal lymphadenectomy with at least 6 nodes examined for accurate staging, because nodal status drives prognosis and adjuvant decisions.

Portal vein embolization first when the anticipated remnant is insufficient; re-image in 3-4 weeks to confirm hypertrophy. Minimally invasive approaches are acceptable at experienced centers for favorably located tumors.

options.label: Resection completed - proceed to margin-directed adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: eCCA staging
nodes.title: Extrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma: Resectability Assessment
nodes.description: Resectability hinges on vascular involvement, longitudinal ductal extent, remnant adequacy, and absence of distant spread.
bullets: Resectable: no distant metastases, no bilateral secondary biliary radical involvement precluding reconstruction, no encasement of bilateral hepatic arteries or main portal bifurcation beyond reconstruction, and adequate future liver remnant.
Unresectable or metastatic: distant metastases, extensive bilateral ductal spread, unreconstructible vascular encasement, inadequate remnant, or prohibitive operative risk.

Selected patients with unresectable perihilar disease (tumor 3 cm or smaller, no metastases) may be evaluated for neoadjuvant chemoradiation followed by liver transplantation under a strict protocol at a transplant center.

options.label: Resectable perihilar or distal disease
Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease

nodes.name: eCCA site
nodes.title: Resectable eCCA: Perihilar versus Distal Site
nodes.description: Operative strategy is dictated by stricture level relative to the cystic duct insertion.
bullets: Perihilar (Klatskin, at or above the cystic duct insertion): classified by Bismuth-Corlette types I-IV to plan the extent of bile duct resection and hepatectomy.
Distal (below the cystic duct insertion, intrapancreatic bile duct): treated by pancreaticoduodenectomy when resectable.
Confirm the level on high-quality MRCP plus EUS before committing to a perihilar versus Whipple operative plan.

options.label: Perihilar cholangiocarcinoma (Klatskin tumor)
Distal cholangiocarcinoma (intrapancreatic bile duct)

nodes.name: Perihilar resection
nodes.title: Perihilar Cholangiocarcinoma: Bile Duct Resection plus Hepatectomy
nodes.description: Extrahepatic bile duct resection combined with (extended) hepatectomy and Roux-en-Y reconstruction, then margin-directed adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Map Bismuth-Corlette type: type I-II requires bile duct resection with Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy; type IIIa/IIIb requires extended right or left hepatectomy en bloc; type IV requires extended hepatectomy and is resectable only with a reconstructible single-sided remnant.
Portal vein embolization when the anticipated future liver remnant is below 30% (normal liver) or below 30-40% (cholestatic or diseased liver); re-image in 3-4 weeks to confirm hypertrophy.

Routine portal lymphadenectomy with at least 6 nodes; frozen section of proximal and distal bile duct margins with further resection when positive if technically feasible. Preoperative biliary drainage of the future remnant lobe reduces cholangitis and post-hepatectomy liver failure.

options.label: Resection completed - proceed to margin-directed adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: Distal resection
nodes.title: Distal Cholangiocarcinoma: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple)
nodes.description: Standard pancreaticoduodenectomy with regional lymphadenectomy, then margin-directed adjuvant therapy.
bullets: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure, pylorus-preserving or classic) with en bloc distal bile duct, duodenum, and pancreatic head resection plus standard regional lymphadenectomy (at least 6 nodes examined).
Preoperative biliary drainage only for cholangitis, severe pruritus, or planned neoadjuvant delay; routine stenting before upfront Whipple increases wound infection risk.
Standard postoperative care: monitor for pancreatic fistula, delayed gastric emptying, and biliary leak; initiate adjuvant capecitabine within 8-12 weeks when recovered.
Record pancreatic fistula risk, bile duct and pancreatic margins (R0 versus R1), and nodal status on synoptic pathology for adjuvant planning.

options.label: Distal resection completed - proceed to margin-directed adjuvant therapy

nodes.name: Adjuvant margin
nodes.title: Resected BTC: Surgical Margin Status
nodes.description: Adjuvant therapy after macroscopically complete resection is driven by microscopic margin status (R0 versus R1) and nodal disease.
bullets: R0 resection (microscopically negative margins): adjuvant capecitabine per BILCAP is the Category 1 preferred standard regardless of nodal status.
R1 resection (microscopically positive margins): adjuvant capecitabine with or without concurrent chemoradiation to the tumor bed and regional nodes.
Start adjuvant therapy within 8-12 weeks of surgery once recovered; restage to exclude early recurrence before starting.

options.label: R0 resection (microscopically negative margins)
R1 resection (microscopically positive margins)

nodes.name: Adjuvant capecitabine
nodes.title: R0 Resected BTC: Adjuvant Capecitabine (BILCAP)
nodes.description: Category 1 preferred adjuvant therapy after R0 resection of gallbladder cancer or cholangiocarcinoma.
bullets: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 orally twice daily on days 1-14 every 21 days for 8 cycles (BILCAP regimen, Category 1 preferred); dose engine calculates patient-specific doses with renal and DPD adjustments.

BILCAP phase III median overall survival 51.1 months per-protocol (49.6 months ITT) versus 36.4 months with observation; benefit held across gallbladder, intrahepatic, perihilar, and distal primaries.
Monitor hand-foot syndrome, diarrhea, cytopenias, and cardiac symptoms; dose-reduce or interrupt per tolerance rather than abandoning therapy early.
Surveillance after completion: history, physical, liver function, CA 19-9, and contrast-enhanced imaging every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months to 5 years.

nodes.name: R1 chemoradiation
nodes.title: R1 Resected BTC: Adjuvant Capecitabine with or without Chemoradiation
nodes.description: Combined-modality adjuvant therapy for microscopically positive margins, targeting the at-risk tumor bed.
bullets: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 orally twice daily days 1-14 every 21 days for 8 cycles as the systemic backbone (BILCAP); dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

Add concurrent chemoradiation for R1 disease: external beam radiotherapy 45-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions to the tumor bed and regional nodes with concurrent infusional 5-fluorouracil or capecitabine as radiosensitizer.
Sequence chemoradiation before or after systemic capecitabine per multidisciplinary plan; prioritize local control of the positive-margin bed in perihilar and distal primaries.
Consider referral for adjuvant clinical trials, especially for node-positive or perineural invasion positive disease.
Surveillance: history, physical, liver function, CA 19-9, and contrast-enhanced imaging every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months to 5 years.

nodes.name: First-line fitness
nodes.title: Advanced BTC: First-Line Fitness and Immunotherapy Eligibility
nodes.description: Fit patients receive gemcitabine plus cisplatin with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade; immunotherapy-ineligible patients receive cytotoxic GemCis alone; frail patients receive single-agent therapy.
bullets: Chemoimmunotherapy candidates: ECOG 0-1, adequate organ function, no active autoimmune disease requiring immunosuppression, no uncontrolled interstitial lung disease, and controlled biliary drainage.
Cytotoxic-only path: immunotherapy contraindicated (autoimmune history, solid-organ transplant, chronic high-dose steroids) but still platinum-eligible with adequate renal function and hearing.
Frail path: ECOG 2 or greater, significant comorbidity, or cisplatin-ineligible with limited reserve; prioritize tolerability and biliary symptom control.

options.label: Fit for chemoimmunotherapy (GemCis plus durvalumab or pembrolizumab)
Immunotherapy contraindicated: GemCis cytotoxic doublet alone
Poor performance status or frail: single-agent therapy

nodes.name: First-line chemoIO
nodes.title: Advanced BTC First-Line: GemCis plus Durvalumab or Pembrolizumab (Category 1 Preferred)
nodes.description: TOPAZ-1 and KEYNOTE-966 chemoimmunotherapy doublets; gemcitabine plus cisplatin backbone with PD-L1 or PD-1 blockade followed by immunotherapy maintenance.
bullets: Preferred option A (TOPAZ-1, Category 1): gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 plus cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days with durvalumab 1500 mg IV day 1 for up to 8 cycles, then durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks maintenance until progression.

Preferred option B (KEYNOTE-966, Category 1): gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 plus cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days with pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1, then pembrolizumab maintenance until progression or 2 years.
Cytotoxic backbone, hydration, antiemetics, and dose holds follow the StewardMD ONCQIS Standard Protocol gi-btc-gem-cis; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
Reassess with contrast-enhanced imaging every 8-12 weeks; maintain biliary stent patency throughout therapy because cholangitis mimics progression.

options.label: First-line therapy started - assess response at restaging

nodes.name: First-line GemCis
nodes.title: Advanced BTC First-Line: Gemcitabine plus Cisplatin Alone (Category 1)
nodes.description: Cytotoxic doublet for patients with immunotherapy contraindications; remains a Category 1 standard per ABC-02.
bullets: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 plus cisplatin 25 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days for up to 8 cycles (maximum 6 months, ABC-02); substitute carboplatin AUC 5 day 1 when cisplatin-ineligible by renal function or hearing.
Dosing, hydration, antiemetics, and day 1/day 8 clearance checks follow the StewardMD ONCQIS Standard Protocol gi-btc-gem-cis; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
Reassess with contrast-enhanced imaging every 8-12 weeks; switch to second-line biomarker-directed or mFOLFOX6 therapy at progression.

options.label: First-line therapy started - assess response at restaging

nodes.name: Frail single agent
nodes.title: Advanced BTC, Poor Performance Status: Gemcitabine or Capecitabine Monotherapy
nodes.description: Tolerability-first single-agent therapy with early best-supportive-care integration for frail patients.
bullets: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days, with dose holds for cytopenias; preferred when biliary function is marginal but marrow reserve is adequate.
Alternative: capecitabine 1000-1250 mg/m2 orally twice daily days 1-14 every 21 days when venous access or infusion visits are limiting; reduce for renal impairment and DPD deficiency.

Integrate best supportive care early: biliary stent surveillance, pain control, nutrition, and goals-of-care review at each cycle. Escalate to doublet only if performance status improves substantially.

options.label: Single-agent therapy started - assess response at restaging

nodes.name: First-line response
nodes.title: Advanced BTC: First-Line Restaging Response
nodes.description: RECIST 1.1 restaging after first-line therapy separates ongoing benefit (continue or maintain) from progression (biomarker-directed subsequent line).
bullets: Disease control (response or stable disease): continue the effective regimen or its immunotherapy maintenance until progression or limiting toxicity.
Progression: confirm true progression versus stent dysfunction or cholangitis, verify molecular profiling results are in hand, and move to biomarker-directed subsequent-line therapy.
Restage with the same contrast-enhanced modality every 8-12 weeks with CA 19-9 trends interpreted only after biliary decompression.

options.label: Disease controlled: response or stable disease
Disease progression on first-line therapy

nodes.name: Continue first-line
nodes.title: Advanced BTC Controlled: Continue Effective First-Line Therapy
nodes.description: Maintain disease control with the responding regimen; reserve subsequent-line options for true progression.
bullets: Chemoimmunotherapy responders: complete planned GemCis cycles then continue durvalumab every 4 weeks or pembrolizumab maintenance until progression, limiting toxicity, or 2 years of pembrolizumab.
GemCis-alone responders: complete up to 8 cycles (6 months maximum) then observe with surveillance imaging; re-challenge is not standard after a treatment-free interval with progression.
Frail single-agent responders: continue at the tolerated dose with supportive care; restage every 8-12 weeks and keep molecular results current for later lines.

nodes.name: Subsequent-line biomarker
nodes.title: Progressed BTC: NGS Biomarker-Directed Subsequent Line
nodes.description: Match the progressing tumor to its actionable alteration from the mandatory molecular profile; biomarker-negative disease receives cytotoxic chemotherapy.
bullets: Use the comprehensive NGS plus FISH/IHC profile ordered at advanced-disease workup; re-biopsy or add ctDNA when tissue is exhausted or acquired resistance is suspected.
Actionable hierarchy: FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement, IDH1 mutation, HER2 amplification/overexpression, BRAF V600E, MSI-H/dMMR, then NTRK/RET fusions and TMB-H.
Biomarker-negative or unknown: proceed directly to mFOLFOX6 (ABC-06 standard) or FOLFIRI; do not delay chemotherapy awaiting repeat profiling.

options.label: FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement detected
IDH1 R132 mutation detected
HER2 overexpression or ERBB2 amplification
BRAF V600E mutation detected
MSI-H or dMMR detected
Other actionable alteration (NTRK fusion, RET fusion, TMB-H)
No actionable alteration (biomarker-negative or unknown)

nodes.name: FGFR2 inhibitor
nodes.title: FGFR2 Fusion or Rearrangement: Pemigatinib or Futibatinib (Category 1)
nodes.description: Selective FGFR inhibition for FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement positive disease, predominantly intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
bullets: Pemigatinib 13.5 mg orally once daily 14 days on / 7 days off in 21-day cycles (FIGHT-202, Category 1); confirm FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement by NGS or FISH before starting.
Alternative: futibatinib 20 mg orally once daily continuously (FOENIX-CCA2, Category 1), including activity after progression on a reversible FGFR inhibitor in selected patients.
Monitor hyperphosphatemia (phosphate binders, dose holds), ocular toxicity (baseline and periodic eye exams for serous retinal detachment), and nail and skin changes.
At acquired resistance, re-profile by tissue or ctDNA for FGFR2 kinase-domain gatekeeper mutations and consider clinical trials.

nodes.name: IDH1 inhibitor
nodes.title: IDH1 R132 Mutation: Ivosidenib (Category 1)
nodes.description: Mutant IDH1 inhibition for previously treated IDH1 R132 mutant cholangiocarcinoma per ClarIDHy.
bullets: Ivosidenib 500 mg orally once daily continuously (ClarIDHy, Category 1) for IDH1 R132 mutant disease progressing after at least one prior systemic line.
ClarIDHy showed progression-free survival benefit with preserved quality of life and a crossover-adjusted overall survival signal; continue until progression or limiting toxicity.
Monitor QTc prolongation (baseline and periodic ECGs with electrolytes), differentiation-syndrome-like symptoms, nausea, and fatigue; hold for QTc above 480 ms.

nodes.name: HER2-directed therapy
nodes.title: HER2 Overexpression or Amplification: Trastuzumab plus Pertuzumab or Zanidatamab
nodes.description: HER2-directed therapy for IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/ISH positive or ERBB2-amplified biliary tract cancer.
bullets: Confirm HER2 status by IHC with reflex ISH, or ERBB2 amplification by NGS; HER2 positivity is enriched in gallbladder cancer and extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
Option A: trastuzumab plus pertuzumab dual blockade (MyPathway HER2-positive BTC cohort) for IHC 3+ or amplified disease.
Option B: zanidatamab bispecific HER2 antibody (HERIZON-BTC-01) for previously treated HER2-positive (IHC 3+, or IHC 2+/ISH positive) disease.
Baseline and periodic LVEF assessment for HER2 antibody therapy; monitor diarrhea and infusion reactions.

nodes.name: BRAF/MEK inhibition
nodes.title: BRAF V600E Mutation: Dabrafenib plus Trametinib
nodes.description: Combined BRAF plus MEK inhibition for BRAF V600E mutant biliary tract cancer per the ROAR basket trial.
bullets: Dabrafenib 150 mg orally twice daily plus trametinib 2 mg orally once daily continuously (ROAR BTC cohort) for confirmed BRAF V600E disease; BRAF inhibitor monotherapy is inadequate because of paradoxical MAPK reactivation.
Monitor pyrexia syndrome (hold both drugs, antipyretics, steroids if severe), LVEF and ocular exams for trametinib, skin toxicity, and QTc.
Re-image every 8-12 weeks; at progression consider re-profiling for MAPK-pathway resistance and clinical trials.

nodes.name: MSI-H immunotherapy
nodes.title: MSI-H or dMMR: Pembrolizumab
nodes.description: Single-agent PD-1 blockade for MSI-H or mismatch-repair-deficient biliary tract cancer.
bullets: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks until progression, limiting toxicity, or 2 years (KEYNOTE-158 MSI-H BTC data); confirm MSI-H by PCR/NGS or dMMR by IHC.
Responses can be durable even after prior chemoimmunotherapy; distinguish pseudoprogression from true progression before abandoning therapy.
Monitor immune-related adverse events (colitis, hepatitis, pneumonitis, endocrinopathies) with early steroid intervention per toxicity guidelines.

nodes.name: Other actionable target
nodes.title: NTRK Fusion, RET Fusion, or TMB-H: Matched Targeted or Immunotherapy
nodes.description: Tumor-agnostic matched therapy for rare actionable alterations in biliary tract cancer.
bullets: NTRK gene fusion: larotrectinib or entrectinib (tumor-agnostic approvals); confirm fusion at RNA level when DNA NGS is equivocal and monitor dizziness, weight gain, and withdrawal pain.
RET fusion: selpercatinib or pralsetinib (tumor-agnostic RET approvals); monitor hypertension, transaminases, and QTc.
TMB-H (at least 10 mutations per megabase): pembrolizumab is a tumor-agnostic option; weigh prior immunotherapy exposure and confirm TMB on a validated assay.
Refer all such rare-alteration cases for molecular tumor board review and clinical trial matching.

nodes.name: Biomarker-negative chemo
nodes.title: Biomarker-Negative Disease: mFOLFOX6 (ABC-06) or FOLFIRI
nodes.description: Cytotoxic second-line standard for biomarker-negative or unknown disease after GemCis-based first-line therapy.
bullets: mFOLFOX6 every 14 days (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 bolus then 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours) plus active symptom control per ABC-06; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

Alternative FOLFIRI every 14 days (irinotecan 180 mg/m2 replacing oxaliplatin) for oxaliplatin-pretreated neuropathy, platinum hypersensitivity, or residual cytopenias; check UGT1A1 when severe neutropenia or diarrhea occurs.
Maintain biliary drainage, reassess every 8-12 weeks, and integrate early palliative care; offer clinical trials at each progression.
